summary: Entry = one income or expense: ID, Date, Description, Category, Amount (int64 cents), Kind
detail: Month is derived from Date; there is no month key. Editing a date into another month moves the entry. Category is free text, never validated against the category list.

summary: Kind = income | expense; one field on Entry, one code path per operation
detail: Direction of money is Kind only. Amount is never negative. Unknown Kind values are rejected by Ledger.Add and make SQLite Load fail loudly instead of coercing to expense.

summary: Category{Name, Kind, Order}: global, not per-month, only for defaults and display
detail: DefaultCategories() seeds the list when the snapshot has none. Add defaults Entry.Category to the first category of its Kind when empty.

summary: Snapshot{Entries, Categories} is the whole persisted state and the only thing crossing the storage seam
detail: Storage interface is Load() (Snapshot, error) and Save(Snapshot) error. Adding a third adapter means implementing two methods.

summary: Two adapters: SQLiteStorage (real, has Close) and MemoryStorage (tests, exposes Snapshot/Saves/LoadErr/SaveErr)
detail: MemoryStorage.Snapshot can be preset before ledger.New to load fixtures. Saves records every Save call; LastSave() returns the latest. SaveErr/LoadErr inject failures.

summary: Clock = func() time.Time injected into the Ledger; all time-dependent behaviour goes through it
detail: Tests pass a fixed clock. fixture.Now (2026-06-15 UTC) is the shared anchor for benchmarks and budget tests.

summary: Ledger is the single owner of every Entry: Entries/Categories read, Add/Update/Remove mutate, Summary/ChartSeries/TotalBalance derive
detail: Constructed with Storage + Clock, loads the snapshot up front. Every mutation persists the full snapshot synchronously and returns the storage error; in-memory state is updated even on save failure so the UI keeps what the user typed and the status bar shows the error. Ledger holds no selected month; month is an explicit argument on every call and the UI model owns the selection.

summary: EntryTable is a view over Ledger.Entries, never a second owner
detail: It holds a copy for cursor and inline editing. The model writes every new/delete/commit back through the Ledger and re-reads. Columns: Date, Description, Category, Amount.

summary: Money is int64 cents everywhere (Amount, Summary, ChartData, TotalBalance); float64 was replaced on 2026-08-29
detail: Reason: float64 gave 0.1+0.2-0.3 != 0 and made Balance==0 checks wrong. Author chose integer cents over tolerance comparisons. Chaos tests TestChaosSummaryBalanceIsExactForCents and TestChaosTotalBalanceAfterManyCents guard it.

summary: SQLite stores amount_cents INTEGER; legacy amount REAL column is kept and backfilled once with ROUND(amount*100)
detail: init() checks columnExists(entries, amount_cents); if absent it ALTERs the table and backfills. Save writes both amount and amount_cents (and month_key when the legacy column exists) so old readers still work. Load reads amount_cents only.

summary: ParseCurrency: last separator is the decimal one, a lone comma is decimal (1,5 = 1.50); FormatCurrency renders $1.234,56
detail: Rejects negatives, NaN/Inf, empty, $$ and malformed grouping like 1,5,. Round-trips FormatCurrency -> ParseCurrency for normal values. Table in pkg/utils/utils_chaos_test.go covers pt-BR and US inputs.

summary: Negative amounts are rejected by Ledger.Add/Update and ParseCurrency; refunds are not modelled
detail: Author decision 2026-08-29: negatives were never intended. Direction is Kind. A negative expense would be a hidden income.

summary: Invalid date/amount on commit keeps the cell in edit mode and shows the parse error in the status bar; a valid value clears it
detail: Author decision 2026-08-29: silently keeping the old value was not intended. Tests: TestChaosInvalidAmountEditSurfacesFeedbackAndKeepsEditing, TestChaosInvalidDateEditSurfacesFeedback.

summary: Table editor consumes msg.Runes (so ç, ã, emoji work) and Backspace deletes one rune, not one byte
detail: Before: only single-byte keys were accepted and Backspace could leave invalid UTF-8 that got persisted.

summary: SQLite opens with PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000 and journal_mode=WAL so two truf instances on one DB coexist
detail: Without it the second instance got SQLITE_BUSY on every save. Empty dbPath now returns an error instead of panicking on dbPath[0].

summary: Every mutation saves the full snapshot: SQLite deletes and reinserts all rows in one transaction
detail: Chosen for simplicity in the ledger spec. Cost is linear in DB size and runs on every Enter in a cell: 92 ms at 10k entries. Issue #5 tracks moving to per-entry upsert/delete.

summary: Go code carries no comments; names do the work (owner preference)
detail: Spec user story 19. When adding code, do not add explanatory comments; rename instead. Short doc lines in the fixture package and test guards are the only tolerated exception.

summary: Never add Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session or Generated-with footers to commits, PRs or issues
detail: Owner instruction 2026-09-01. History was rewritten on 2026-09-01 to strip existing trailers from all branches.

summary: .gitattributes forces LF for all text and *.go; gofmt -l must be empty in CI
detail: Windows checkouts with core.autocrlf=true show CRLF in the working tree; the index is LF, so gofmt on Linux CI is stable.

summary: Adversarial tests live in *_chaos_test.go per package; a finding fixed later is re-armed by deleting its t.Skip(CHAOS: ...) line
detail: 41 chaos tests, 0 skipped as of 2026-08-29. Timing-sensitive tests check a raceEnabled flag (set by a //go:build race file) and skip under -race.

summary: Ledger spec (2026-08-29, implemented, file not committed): Ledger owns entries, replaces the old models package and the UI-side double ownership
detail: Problem: add/edit/delete used to touch the table and month data separately and rely on a later sync, causing duplicate rows and accidental deletes. Solution: Ledger with Storage+Clock injection. Out of scope then: month navigation UI, category validation, Categories/Settings panels, layout function, the Fin/ project. Tests exercise the Ledger only through its interface with the memory adapter. Specs are written locally and never committed; this entry is the surviving record.

summary: Keys: Tab menu/content, up/down or k/j navigate, [ ] or h l previous/next month on tables, Enter open view or edit row, n new, d delete, Esc back to Overview, PgUp/PgDn chart range 3..24 months, q quit
detail: While editing: Tab/Enter next column, Esc cancels, Backspace rune-aware. Menu items: overview, income, expenses, categories, settings (last two are placeholders).

summary: Bubble Tea Model: ledger, month (starts at clock month, shifted by [ ] on tables), menu, chart, statusBar, incomeTable, expenseTable, focusedPanel, currentView, chartMonths, width/height, err
detail: Views: Overview, Income, Expenses, Categories, Settings. refreshChart() and refreshTables() re-read the Ledger. Status bar renders TotalBalance and m.err. Dates display and parse as 01/02/2006 (US month/day/year).

summary: Issue #3: tables are stuck on the current month; add [ / ] month navigation using utils.PreviousMonth/NextMonth (already exist, unused)
detail: Show active month in the panel title, reset cursor, refresh chart anchor. AddMonths clamps to month end so Jan 31 navigation is safe.

summary: Issue #4: main.go only understands --seed; add --help, --version, --db via the flag package; unknown flags exit 2
detail: --version reads main.version injected with -ldflags -X main.version=TAG from release.yml; also gives CI a headless startup-time probe.

summary: Issue #5: full-snapshot save costs 92 ms / 162k allocs at 10k entries and ~1 MB per Add in memory; move to per-entry upsert/delete on the Storage seam
detail: Options ranked: 1) Put(Entry)/Delete(id) on Storage, 2) diff against last snapshot, 3) debounce (risky). Only two adapters exist.

summary: Issue #6: ChartSeries(24) costs 5 ms / ~700 allocs (1793 after int-cents) at 10k entries and is recomputed per frame on the overview
detail: Options: cache rendered chart string until data/resize changes; bucket entries by month incrementally in the Ledger; pre-sort by date to drop per-entry sameMonth checks.

summary: Local baseline (10k entries, master after int-cents): overview frame 2.2 ms/2.4 MB, table frame 0.8 ms, ChartSeries24 4.9 ms, Save10k 92-146 ms, Load10k 20 ms, open+load 1k 3.5 ms
detail: Allocations rose after int-cents: EntriesMonth 17->48, Summary 24->62, ChartSeries 696->1793, TotalBalance 2->6. Time unchanged. Likely the new currency formatting path; not investigated.

summary: TestPerfBudget*: median of 200 frames with 10k entries must stay under 25 ms overview / 10 ms table (lax) or 7 ms / 3 ms with TRUF_PERF_STRICT=1 (CI perf job)
detail: Skipped under -race and -short. Binary size gate: stripped linux/amd64 build must be under 12 MB (about 8 MB today).

summary: go run ./cmd/truf | --seed for sample data | go test ./... | go test -run ^$ -bench . -benchmem ./... | TRUF_PERF_STRICT=1 go test -run PerfBudget -v ./internal/ui/
detail: Data lives in ~/.truf/truf.db. Module path is github.com/gabriel-luiz/truf. go.mod pins go 1.22.0; local toolchain is 1.25.x.

summary: internal/fixture builds deterministic data: fixture.Entries(n, months), fixture.Snapshot(n, months), fixture.Now; setAmount generic keeps it compiling for int64 or float64 Amount
detail: Every third entry is income (Salary), the rest expense (Food). IDs fx-000000 onward. Descriptions contain accented text on purpose.

summary: ci.yml: lint (gofmt, vet, go mod tidy no-op) -> test (ubuntu+windows, -race on linux) and perf (binary size gate, strict budgets, benchmarks + benchstat vs PR base, job summary + artifact)
detail: Triggers: push and pull_request on master. Concurrency cancels superseded runs. Perf results are written to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY.

summary: release.yml: on tag v* cross-compiles linux/darwin (amd64+arm64) and windows/amd64 with CGO_ENABLED=0 -trimpath -ldflags -s -w, writes SHA256SUMS.txt, publishes a GitHub Release with generated notes
detail: To release: git tag v0.1.0 then git push origin v0.1.0. sqlite is modernc (pure Go) so no CGO anywhere.

summary: Dependabot runs weekly with one grouped PR for Go modules (go-deps) and one for actions (actions)
detail: First run on 2026-09-02 opened 6 separate PRs because actions were not grouped yet; fixed in PR #13.

summary: actions/setup-go v7 sets GOTOOLCHAIN=local; go install of a tool needing a newer Go than go.mod fails. Benchstat is installed with GOTOOLCHAIN=auto for that reason
detail: Symptom: benchstat@latest requires go >= 1.26.0 (running go 1.22.0; GOTOOLCHAIN=local). Seen on Dependabot PR #10.

summary: -race makes the 20k-row save ~30x slower (8.7 s); any wall-clock assertion must skip when raceEnabled
detail: Pattern: package-level var raceEnabled = false in a normal test file, plus a //go:build race file whose init sets it true.

summary: Chaos run 2026-08-29: 40 attacks, 19 KILLED (Inf amount bricked the app, multibyte input dropped, float money, SQLITE_BUSY, silent discard...) all fixed same day; 21 SURVIVED promoted to regressions
detail: Report kept locally in chaos-reports/ (gitignored). Fixes merged via PR #2 on 2026-09-02.

summary: PR #1 CI pipeline + perf; PR #2 chaos fixes; PR #13 benchstat GOTOOLCHAIN + Dependabot grouping; PR #14 setup-go v7 (replaces Dependabot #10); Dependabot #7 #8 #9 #11 #12 merged
detail: Default branch is master. Repo GabrielL915/truf, public. gh CLI installed at C:/Program Files/GitHub CLI/gh.exe; jq via winget.

summary: Direct deps after 2026-09-02: bubbletea 1.3.10, lipgloss 1.1.0, ntcharts 0.5.1, google/uuid 1.6.0, modernc.org/sqlite 1.57.0
detail: ntcharts draws the balance chart; lipgloss styles; modernc sqlite is CGO-free.

summary: Before exploring code, run scripts/kb.sh search <terms>; add new decisions/findings with scripts/kb.sh add; keep summaries one line so hits are cheap to read
detail: File: docs/knowledge/truf.jsonl, one JSON object per line: id, type, topic, tags, summary, detail, refs, date. Types: concept, decision, convention, spec, howto, perf, issue, gotcha, history, reference. Specs are never committed: distil each one into a spec.* entry. CI runs scripts/kb.sh check (valid JSON, unique ids, every ref exists).

summary: Specs are drafted locally (docs/specs/, gitignored) and never committed; what matters is distilled into a spec.* entry in the knowledge base
detail: Owner decision 2026-09-02. The ledger spec was removed from the tree the same day; spec.ledger keeps its substance.

summary: jq.exe on Windows emits CRLF; strip the trailing CR from any jq output consumed by bash (kb.sh check does) and normalise the JSONL with sed s/\r$//
detail: Symptom: every ref reported as missing in kb.sh check although the files exist.

summary: Month navigation: [ / ] or h / l shift the active month on Income/Expenses (content focus only, ignored while editing); title shows 'Income — Feb 2026', cursor resets, chart anchor and status range follow
detail: Model.shiftMonth(delta) uses utils.AddMonths on m.month (always first of month), resets both table cursors, refreshTables (EntryTable.SetMonth) and refreshChart. New entries in a non-current month are dated the 1st (newEntryDate). Closes issue #3.
